q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis

**(a) Time left until resolution**

Today is August 22, 2026. Q2 FY2027 corresponds to Q2 of NVIDIA's fiscal year 2027. NVIDIA's fiscal year ends in January, so:
- Q1 FY2027: Feb-April 2026 (earnings released May 20, 2026)
- Q2 FY2027: May-July 2026 (earnings would be released ~August 2026)

The Q2 FY2027 earnings release has likely already occurred or is imminent (within days). Time to resolution: essentially 0 days (the earnings have probably already been announced or will be announced within the current trading week).

**(b) Most likely outcome and why**

NVIDIA already provided forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 in its May 20, 2026 Q1 earnings release: **$91.0 billion ± 2%**, which translates to a range of **$89.2 billion to $92.8 billion**.

The most likely outcome is that the actual Q2 FY2027 revenue guidance (or actual results) will fall within or very close to this guided range. NVIDIA typically provides relatively accurate guidance—they have a strong track record of either meeting or slightly exceeding their own forward guidance.

Analysts' consensus estimate of $91.8-$91.9 billion falls squarely in the middle-to-upper portion of the company's guided range, suggesting the market expects NVIDIA to deliver near the upper end of guidance or slightly above it.

**(c) What would push the value lower?**

- Unexpected Data Center weakness or customer inventory corrections
- Geopolitical events further restricting China revenue (already assumed at $0)
- Yield issues or manufacturing constraints limiting supply
- Macro weakness affecting cloud provider capex spending
- However, given the guidance was already provided, actual results would need a significant miss to fall meaningfully below $89.2B

**(d) What would push the value higher?**

- Better-than-expected demand for Blackwell GPUs or H100 inventory liquidation
- Accelerated AI adoption driving higher customer orders
- China revenue somehow contributing (unlikely given current restrictions already factored in)
- Mix shift toward higher-margin products
- Upside surprise in cloud provider capex spending

However, NVIDIA typically guides conservatively and management tends to deliver within or slightly above guidance rather than dramatically exceed it.

**(e) Base rate or historical reference values**

The only concrete base rate provided in the research is NVIDIA's own forward guidance: **$91.0 billion ± 2%** ($89.2B - $92.8B range). This was officially stated for Q2 FY2027 in the May 20, 2026 earnings release.

Q1 FY2027 actual results were $81.6 billion, representing an 85% YoY increase and 20% sequential growth, which suggests strong momentum into Q2.

---

# Reasoning

The question asks for NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release regarding revenue. This guidance has already been publicly disclosed ($91.0B ± 2%). The most likely scenario is that when earnings are announced (imminently or already), the company will either:

1. Reiterate the $91.0B guidance with ±2% range, or
2. Provide updated guidance for Q3 FY2027 (not Q2, which is already closed)

If this question is asking for the **actual Q2 FY2027 results** (not forward guidance for Q3), those results should be announced within days if not already. Given the guided range and analyst consensus, actual results should cluster around $89.2B-$92.8B with the most likely outcome near $91.0B-$91.9B.

The range provided ($99.5B - $115.5B) seems to contemplate scenarios significantly above current guidance, which would represent a major upside surprise. Given NVIDIA's conservative guidance practices, outcomes above $93B would be unusual but not impossible in a scenario of dramatically accelerating AI demand.

My probability distribution:
- 60% likelihood: Revenue within guided range ($89.2B-$92.8B)
- 20% likelihood: Results slightly above guidance ($92.8B-$95B)
- 15% likelihood: Results slightly below guidance ($87B-$89.2B)
- 5% likelihood: Significant upside ($95B+) or downside ($<$87B)

The median should reflect the midpoint of the guided range with slight upside bias based on analyst consensus and momentum.

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA has already provided forward guidance for its Q2 FY2027 revenue in its Q1 FY2027 earnings release on May 20, 2026. The company expects revenue to be $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). This guidance implies a range between $89.2 billion and $92.8 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). NVIDIA's outlook does not assume any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), a stance consistent with the previous year due to U.S. licensing requirements for H20 chips [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).

Analysts' average estimate for Q2 FY2027 revenue is around $91.9 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/) or $91.846 billion [hudson-labs.com](https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/nvidia-q2-2027-earnings-preview-nvda-revenue-guidance-key-factors), which falls within NVIDIA's guided range. The company reported record Q1 FY2027 revenue of $81.6 billion, an 85% increase year-over-year and 20% sequentially [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/).
